nodes.label: hierarchy/block_spans.py
nodes.rationale: Recomputes split boundaries with the SAME expression as reconcile.reconcile rather than a paraphrase, fits nothing and calls no model — so the figure cannot drift from the code it depicts.

nodes.label: Four-block split (fit / validation / calibration / test)
nodes.rationale: Not four spans of eight weeks: three blocks of eight weeks plus a 230-day fit span four times longer than any other. A figure drawn to scale should show that asymmetry because the reader's likely misreading is that the blocks are comparable.

nodes.label: n=56 is the calibration block, not the test block
nodes.rationale: The two are adjacent, equal in nominal length and easy to confuse; the test block is 57 days because the boundary is inclusive at both ends.

nodes.label: eval/exchangeability_scores.csv (per-day conformity scores)
nodes.rationale: A persistence change, not a recompute: venue_report gained a collect list, and the JSON's venues block is byte-identical to the committed one — the verification that no number moved.

nodes.label: functional_pair untrimmed-frame defect (R4)
nodes.rationale: functional_pair calls build_features (untrimmed) where fold_vectors calls ladder._load_feats (trimmed). Its own line-47 comment states 273/260/205 while it produces 273/266/205 — intent recorded in source, not implemented in code, so it is an oversight rather than a deliberate divergence.

nodes.label: trim_to_active
nodes.rationale: Exists so training windows are not padded with structural zeros — 'otherwise every model trivially wins by predicting zero'. The hazard applies at the head of a series as much as at the tail.

nodes.label: One-line fix proposed, not executed
nodes.rationale: It re-runs an experiment and moves a reported number, so it goes to the human. If declined, Methods must state that the two frames differ by oversight — a worse sentence than the fix is a cost.
